en: The Apadāna of the Elder Pañcadīpaka Bījanī Vagga, Chapter 7 I was a merchant in the city of Benares, and I possessed five lamps. Having offered them at the foot of the Bodhi tree, I made this aspiration: "May I become a lamp for the world. Having performed that deed, I was reborn in the realm of the Thirty-three gods. There, as a result of that deed, I shone with great splendor. From there, passing away, I was reborn in the human world. There, too, I became a lamp for the world; I dispelled the darkness and brought light to the world. Now, having passed away from here, I have been reborn in the realm of Tusita. There, too, I am a lamp for the world; I dispel the darkness and bring light to the world. By means of that very deed, I have attained the state of an Arhat. I have reached the end of suffering and am free from all defilements. I have crossed over the ocean of existence and am liberated from the cycle of rebirth. I have attained the goal and fulfilled my purpose. I have done what was to be done and shall not be born again. Thus did the Elder Pañcadīpaka speak his own ancient history. It was heard by the Buddha, the Blessed One, who said: "Well said, well said, monk! You have spoken well, monk. Thus the Buddha praised him. This is the Apadāna of the Elder Pañcadīpaka. “Having placed faith in the True Dhamma of Padumuttara Buddha, who is compassionate toward all living beings,
I held the view that there is a self.
Having surrounded the Bodhi tree, I offered a gift of a lamp.
Having faith, I then offered lamps;
wherever I was reborn, I did so.
Whether in the divine realm or the human world,
they hold aloft lamps in the sky:
this is the fruit of the gift of a lamp.
Passing through walls and passing through rocks,
having crossed over the mountain,
for a hundred leagues all around—
I experienced that vision.
By the remainder of that karma,
I have attained the destruction of the taints.
I bear my final body within the teaching of the Lord of Bipeds;
in thirty-four hundred aeons—
Known by the name Satacakkhu,
they were kings of great majesty,
universal monarchs of mighty power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so on]...
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Pañcadīpaka spoke these verses.
This is the seventh legend of the elder Pañcadīpaka.
